approach.method_basis: The Parent is a task-local graph genetic algorithm whose evaluation budget is spent by a Gaussian-process Thompson sampler, with one stagnation reflex already added. It keeps every molecule scored in the current session in an archive and the best sixty-four in a breeding population, draws breeding parents from high score quantiles, and builds a fresh field of one hundred and sixty de novo offspring for each announced batch of ten by connected-fragment crossover with an optional finishing edit or by a short random walk of atom, bond and ring edits, rejecting anything that is not a single ordinary connected graph, is already known, or introduces a sulfur environment outside a fixed neutral envelope more often than its own scored parents did. It fits a Gaussian process to the accepted scores of this session only, using integer-count radius-two Morgan fingerprints and a generalized Tanimoto kernel with scores recentred and rescaled by their running mean and spread, draws one correlated posterior sample per batch position over the whole field, and sends to the oracle the ten sequential sampled maxima, removing each winner before the next position. On top of that it watches its own progress: it counts announced batches that did not raise the session's best score, and once three consecutive such batches have passed it offers the sampler only the forty members of the unchanged field that the fitted model ranks highest by posterior mean, so a stalled batch is drawn from the top quarter of model value instead of the whole field. That sharpened state is fragile by construction: the very first batch that raises the best score, by any margin at all, hands the whole field back, and the counter starts again from zero.
approach.novelty: This node changes how long the sharpened state lasts, and nothing else. The regime still begins after three consecutive non-improving announced batches, but it is no longer surrendered to a single lucky batch: once entered it governs every following announced batch until the session has produced two consecutive improving announced batches, and only then is the inherited full-field behaviour restored exactly and the counters cleared. One hysteresis value is fixed before the run, with no adaptation during a run, no per-task value and no sweep. This is the first intervention on this Parent, which has no earlier Children, and the first on this route to touch the duration of the stagnation regime rather than its content; the same exit rule is being tried in parallel on one other stall-time element, on a different Parent, so the arms are read side by side rather than summed. All eight arms tried on this Parent's own Parent at the same trigger changed what a stalled batch does - how many candidates were bred for it, how wide its sampled residual was, how long its mutation walks ran, which of its candidates were eligible, or nothing at all in the law-free reference draw - while every one of them kept the inherited one-improvement release. It is also, deliberately, the element the Parent's own source method supplies and the Parent's own plan declined: the trust-region method this route borrows its stagnation counter from leaves a sharpened state only after repeated measured success, and the Parent adopted the failure counter while keeping the one-improvement release. Holding the regime roughly doubles the exposure of the element that is already measured to help per batch, and it concentrates that increase on the score-compressed task the round's brief targets, whose tiny improvements were exactly what kept releasing the regime. The experiment therefore discriminates: if the Parent's margin is a property of the eligibility law it should grow with exposure, and if it was one favourable path draw - or if holding a sharpened state through a long stall is itself harmful, as the Parent's three long episodes hint - it should not.

observed_bottleneck: The code Parent n-61b9b3bfb40d releases its stall regime at the first improving announced batch of any size, so the one behaviour it demonstrably does well is confined to a fifth of the budget and cannot accumulate. Its own audited receipts show the restriction working: 88 of 435 announced batches were restricted, not one of their 880 oracle calls went to a candidate ranked 40 or worse of 160 by posterior mean (against 218 of 910 for the Anchor n-1744a1494180), and the restricted batches realized more per batch than the Anchor's stalled batches (best-so-far increments 0.006216 per restricted batch against 0.005237; mean in-regime offspring score 0.412585 against 0.404629; 31 in-regime incumbent improvements against 28; positive original-parent gain mass 1.678700 against 1.643581). Recomputing the regime from the Parent's own published stall_regime_state and stall_regime_update receipts (runs/SPIRAL2/nodes/n-61b9b3bfb40d/seed-0|1|2/logs/<task>.log, 29 announced batches per session) locates the limit in the exit rule rather than in the entry rule: its 88 restricted batches fall in 29 episodes, 25 of which are ended by a single improving announced batch and only 4 of which survive to the end of their session, and the improvements that release them are small (median 0.010361, minimum 0.000410, 8 of 25 below 0.005 and 11 below 0.01). Only 13 of 15 sessions are exposed at all, 12 of 15 keep their longest episode at five batches or fewer, and the task the round-40 brief targets is the least reached - median_2 is restricted in only 10 of its 87 announced batches, because its per-batch best-so-far increments are tiny (seed medians 0.00235/0.00308/0.00433) and any improvement, however small, resets the counter. The consequence is the open question recorded against this Parent: its +0.010577 complete matched panel rests on two sitagliptin_mpo cells (+0.001013 without seed 1, -0.003826 without both) and stands above a single law-free path reference at the same trigger (n-47993ce5d053, -0.001735, single cells swinging -0.033955 to +0.040951), so at a fifth of the budget the design cannot separate a law effect from one favourable draw. The same receipts also carry the opposite warning, which this exit rule puts directly to the test: the three cells whose restricted episode ran long (zaleplon_mpo seed 1 held 17 consecutive batches, zaleplon_mpo seed 0 eight, drd2_docking seed 2 nine) all lost ground (-0.035318, -0.035875, -0.008280) while every gaining cell kept its longest episode at five batches or fewer.

adoptions.applicability: The borrowed element addresses exactly this Parent's measured limit: its own receipts show 38 improving announced batches occurring inside an episode and releasing the regime immediately, 88 of 435 batches restricted, and the brief's target task reached in only 10 of its 87 batches because any improvement resets the counter, while the restricted batches it does reach realize more per batch than the Anchor's stalled batches. Adopting the success-counter release raises exposure to a predicted 164 of 435 without touching the entry rule or the allocation law, which is what makes the exposure-scaling question testable here. The source's own warning transfers too: because it also expands and restarts, it never holds a sharpened state indefinitely, which is why this node's falsifier treats falling per-batch in-regime gain under long holds as evidence against the adjustment.
adoptions.borrowed_element: The success-counter release rule: a state entered after consecutive measured failures is not left at the first improvement but only after tau_succ consecutive successes, with the counters reset at the state change, so the sharpened state persists across batches while the search is not repeatedly improving.

deviations.adopted_setting: tau_succ = 2 consecutive improving announced batches, bound once before evaluation with no mid-run adaptation, no per-task value and no sweep.
deviations.paper_setting: tau_succ = 3 consecutive successes is the TuRBO-1 default for leaving the sharpened state.
deviations.reason: Two is the minimal hysteresis and keeps the exposure change bounded (a predicted 164 of 435 announced batches rather than more) and the measured must-preserve risk on zaleplon_mpo smaller, where the Parent's mean 0.437595 leaves about 0.0008 of the registered 0.02 margin against the Anchor's 0.456809. The frozen Search Policy review records this same deviation.

deviations.adopted_setting: An improving announced batch, defined exactly as the inherited trigger does: the session's best-so-far after the batch exceeds the value held when that batch was announced.
deviations.paper_setting: A success is defined per candidate, and in the batch setting as at least one evaluation in the batch improving the incumbent.
deviations.reason: This is the campaign's already measured definition on this route, and it coincides with the source's batch-level definition, so the contrast isolates the release rule instead of introducing a second new trigger.

deviations.adopted_setting: The regime is binary: reaching tau_succ restores the Parent's inherited unrestricted behaviour exactly, and re-entry needs the inherited three consecutive non-improving announced batches again. No expansion, no size ladder and no geometry.
deviations.paper_setting: Reaching tau_succ consecutive successes doubles the trust region, and the region shrinks again after tau_fail failures within a continuous geometry bounded by L_min and L_max.
deviations.reason: A freshly bred molecular graph pool has no coordinate box to expand, and a size ladder would add a second adaptive parameter to one registered element. The inherited eligibility size M = 40 of 160 is held fixed so only the duration changes.

deviations.adopted_setting: No restart and no escalation: a regime that is never released simply holds to the end of the session, as this Parent already does in one of its own cells.
deviations.paper_setting: A region whose side length falls below L_min is discarded and the search is re-initialized from a fresh region.
deviations.reason: A restart would discard the accepted archive and survivor population that this lineage's measured positive components depend on, and a release or escalation rule for long stalls is a different intervention that this result is designed to inform rather than contain.

deviations.adopted_setting: The entry rule is unchanged at K = 3 consecutive non-improving announced batches, the value already measured across eight same-trigger arms on this Parent's own Parent.
deviations.paper_setting: tau_fail = ceil(d/q) is set from the problem dimension and the batch size.
deviations.reason: A dimension-based tolerance has no meaning for molecular graphs, and holding the entry rule fixed keeps the eight same-trigger arms and this node's pre-divergence path comparable.

adoptions.implementation_change: In the candidate's optimize.py the stall regime becomes persistent state: Evolution gains self.stall_regime_active and self.stall_success_streak, Evolution.suggest computes stalled = self.stall_regime_active or self.stall_streak >= 3 and stores the flag, and Evolution.observe counts consecutive improving announced batches while the regime is active and clears the regime and both counters when that count reaches CONFIG['posterior_selector']['stall_exit_improving_batches'] = 2. The inherited top-forty posterior-mean availability mask, the GP, the draws and their consumption count, the Cholesky factor, the residual scale, the per-pick mask update and the first-index tie rule are untouched.

literature_review.conclusion: The ticket's frozen basis and the Parent's inherited review already carried this source; this review read its full text again to fix the one element now being adopted and to separate it from what was adopted before. The Parent took the failure counter and refused the release rule; this node takes the release rule and changes nothing else, with tau_succ = 2 rather than the paper's default 3 to bound the exposure change and the measured must-preserve risk. The benchmark source fixes how the result must be read: five independent runs and an explicit non-determinism caveat there, against three protocol-owned seeds here, which is why the panel is read against both the code Parent and the trigger-matched law-free path reference and why no tau_succ sweep follows either outcome. The decision to spend this position on duration rather than on another law rests on internal evidence: in the Parent's own receipts the regime covers 88 of 435 announced batches, 38 regime-internal improving batches release it immediately, the round-40 target task median_2 reaches it in 10 of 87 batches, and the restricted batches that do happen realize more per batch than the Anchor's. Literature origin is not permission to continue: one complete exposed panel ends this adjustment, and if the exit rule activates exactly while the per-batch in-regime magnitudes or the complete panel do not hold up, the exposure-scaling claim is recorded as refuted with no sweep and no re-thresholding.

sources.applicability: This Parent already implements the failure counter (K = 3 consecutive non-improving announced batches) but leaves the sharpened state on the first improving batch of any size, which is the opposite of the source's success-counter semantics; the exit rule and one tau_succ are the only elements adopted. The source's batch-level definition of success coincides with the campaign's already registered improving-batch definition, so no new trigger is introduced. None of its geometry, rates, restart rule or benchmark results is campaign evidence.
sources.finding: Read directly for this node: each trust region keeps counters of consecutive successes and failures, a success being a candidate that improves on the incumbent and, in the batch setting, 'an improvement from at least one evaluation in the batch'; if no point in a batch improves the best solution the success counter is reset to zero and the failure counter increases. The region is halved after tau_fail consecutive failures and doubled after tau_succ consecutive successes, and 'we reset the success and failure counters to zero after we change the size of the TR'. The TuRBO-1 defaults are tau_succ = 3 and tau_fail = ceil(d/q), with L_init 0.8, L_min 2^-7 and L_max 1.6, and a region whose side length falls below L_min is discarded and re-initialized.

hypothesis: Success-counter hysteresis on the exit of the stall regime: the regime is still entered exactly when the session's counter of consecutive non-improving announced batches reaches K=3, but once active it governs every following announced batch until the session has produced tau_succ=2 consecutive improving announced batches, at which point the Parent's inherited unrestricted behaviour is restored exactly and both counters are cleared; a single improving announced batch no longer releases the regime. Everything the regime does when active is inherited unchanged - the initial availability mask of the correlated Thompson allocation is restricted to the M=40 members of the unchanged 160-member fresh pool with the highest fitted posterior mean ordered by (-posterior mean, pool index), and the pool target, the standard-normal array's shape, order and consumption count, the Cholesky factor and jitter, the residual scale, the per-pick mask update and the first-index tie rule are exactly the Parent's. The new state is two integers maintained from this session's own accepted scores at announcement and at observation; it consumes no randomness and reads no task identity, no absolute score level and no other session.

finding_summary.headline: Holding the stall regime nearly doubled its exposure exactly as built, but per-batch gain fell and the panel lost 0.0079 to the Parent
finding_summary.insights:
The question was whether the Parent's +0.0106 came from the top-forty rule itself, in which case it should grow with exposure, or from one favourable path. The answer points to the path. Exposure nearly doubled as designed and the rule stayed exact. Even so, the per-batch increment fell and the panel dropped below the Parent's. The whole loss sits in the two sitagliptin_mpo cells that had carried the Parent's margin, while the other twelve cells are flat. That pattern is what to expect if the Parent's margin came mainly from where those two sessions happened to go. It is not what to expect if the restriction gains value with every additional stalled batch it governs. The registered falsifier therefore triggered, and the exposure-scaling claim is recorded as refuted. The verdict concerns the claim, not the implementation, which ran exactly. By the registered rule this ends the hold direction: no sweep of the exit count, no per-task value, no re-thresholded entry and no change to the eligible-set size follows.

The run also shows how holding fails. A held batch comes right after an improvement, so the search sits next to a fresh incumbent. There, the top quarter of the posterior mean still yields good molecules (in-regime accepted quality kept its advantage over the Anchor) but only small steps. Holding raised the share of improving batches and shrank each improvement, and almost all in-episode gain came in the first three or four batches. On median_2, the score-compressed target, the result was 2.6 times the restricted exposure and many tiny incumbent steps, with no movement of the three-seed mean beyond path noise. The bottleneck there is not how long the restriction lasts. This fits the molecular review of this node. Late-session proposals are mostly one-atom halogen and substituent permutations of a single scaffold that the objectives barely separate, so a sharpened mean-ranked set keeps harvesting near-ties instead of crossing a plateau. That link is consistent with the data but was not measured directly.

The evidence now leans away from longer holds and toward shorter ones. A rule that releases or escalates a restricted episode after a few batches without progress is the natural next distinguishing test. It is the part of the borrowed trust-region method that neither this node nor its Parent adopted. The case is not clean, however. Among cells with an episode of eight batches or more, four gained and four lost against the Anchor. The largest loss, sitagliptin_mpo seed 0, followed a single held batch that changed two picks and then an eleven-batch terminal stall that the inherited rule would also have restricted.

Two things remain open. This round's law-free reference, held at the same regime, has not finished, so the size of pure path noise at this exposure is still known from a single draw. The sibling arm that holds the regime around the fourfold fresh pool will show whether the exposure law also fails on a second element. The must-preserve constraint held, but zaleplon_mpo has only 0.002 of its 0.02 margin left.
finding_summary.results:
The hold ran exactly as registered in all fifteen sessions. Entry was untouched: every one of the 22 regime entries came at exactly three consecutive non-improving announced batches. Every one of the 15 exits came at the second of two consecutive improving batches, never after a single one, and the other 7 episodes ran to the end of their session. The logged regime state agreed with an independent recount from the run's own scores in all 435 announced batches. Exposure rose from the Parent's 88 restricted batches to 162 of 435, against a forecast of 164. 75 of those batches were held batches, which the inherited rule would have released. 41 improving batches inside a regime no longer ended it. On the target task, median_2, restricted batches rose from 10 to 26 (forecast 28). The inherited top-forty restriction itself stayed exact. Not one of 1,620 in-regime picks went to a candidate ranked 40th or worse by posterior mean, and unrestricted picks stayed at the Parent's level (29.6% ranked 40 or worse, against 28.7%). Every session was the Parent's run, molecule for molecule, up to its own first held batch. Each first held batch fell exactly where it was forecast. The two deco_hop sessions that never stall (seeds 0 and 2) and the zaleplon_mpo seed-1 session reproduced the Parent record for record. At the first held batches the swap matched the forecast to the digit: 47 of 130 positions and 42 picks changed, and the dropped picks had averaged 0.321 against 0.400 for the kept ones.

The extra exposure did not pay per batch. Summed over the regime, every quantity grew because there were more batches: best-so-far increments rose from 0.547 to 0.767, positive gain over the generating parent from 1.68 to 3.11, and incumbent improvements from 31 to 65. Per restricted batch, the increment fell 24%, from 0.00622 to 0.00474. Positive gain mass stayed flat (0.01919 against 0.01908) and the mean in-regime offspring score was marginally lower (0.4122 against 0.4126). Reweighting the Parent's per-task rates to the Child's heavier share of slow-moving tasks still gives 0.00571 per batch, so the drop is not only a task-mix effect. Task by task, in-regime accepted quality stayed about +0.028 above the Anchor's stalled batches (the Parent's figure was +0.031). The molecules the regime chose were as good as before; they just moved the incumbent less. The held batches were the weakest: 0.00423 per batch, against 0.00518 for the batches the inherited rule also restricts. They improved more often (40% of held batches against 30%) but by less each time: an improving held batch added 0.0106 on average, against 0.0173 for counter-triggered batches and 0.0219 in the Parent. Within an episode, gain came early. Pooled across sessions, the first three batches of an episode averaged 0.0097, 0.0063 and 0.0084. The fourth averaged 0.0041 and the fifth nothing. Batches six to ten averaged 0.0019, and batches eleven and later 0.0038. Increments traceable to in-regime offspring and their descendants fell from 1.142 to 1.079, and increments after each session's first stall fell from 1.198 to 1.079.

On the complete matched panel the mean fell from the Parent's 0.6070 to 0.5991, a paired delta of -0.0079. The seed macros moved -0.0170, -0.0071 and +0.0002. With any single cell left out the delta stays negative, between -0.0098 and -0.0011. Seven cells rose, four fell and four were unchanged. The whole loss sits in sitagliptin_mpo: seed 0 lost 0.103 and seed 1 lost 0.045, the two cells that had carried the Parent's own margin. The other twelve cells average +0.0010. Against the Anchor the panel is +0.0026, nominally above the +0.002 bar. That figure rests on seed macros of -0.0104, +0.0150 and +0.0033 and lies inside the law-free path reference's seed spread (-0.0127 to +0.0080). Without sitagliptin_mpo seed 1 it becomes -0.0043. median_2 missed its target. Its three-seed mean of 0.2260 is +0.0033 against the Anchor, below the +0.010 required, and -0.0028 against the Parent, and its seed-2 cell (0.2264) is below the Anchor's 0.2323. All four protected tasks held their margins against the Anchor: deco_hop +0.0030 (margin 0.02), drd2_docking -0.0035 (margin 0.03), sitagliptin_mpo +0.0286 (margin 0.02) and zaleplon_mpo -0.0180 (margin 0.02, leaving 0.0020 of headroom).

molecular.headline: Halogen-decorated fused heteroaromatics plus one saturated aminal amine family; leaders put halogen on N and O, never on a CF3
molecular.overall_character: Across the five objectives this node proposed 870 optimizer molecules each (4,350 in total; seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 accepted observations per session of which ten are the shared initial records). All 4,350 parse as valid neutral molecules; none was unparseable. They are medium-sized and heavily cyclic: mean 24.5-31.5 heavy atoms, MW 363-464, 3.1-4.6 rings and 2.1-3.5 aromatic rings per molecule, consistent with the digest string counters (ring_closure_rate 0.974-0.991, aromatic_atom_rate 0.974-0.983, branch_rate 0.975-0.987). Elaboration is almost entirely peripheral decoration of a fused heteroaromatic or bridged polycyclic core with small groups: methyl, ethyl, propyl, methoxy, hydroxymethyl, acetyl, formyl and above all halogen (digest halogen_rate 0.80-0.99 on four objectives, 0.11 on the fifth). Halogen lands on heteroatoms as readily as on carbon: 1,130 of the 4,350 proposals carry a halogen on a non-carbon atom and 627 carry one on an aromatic nitrogen, while exactly 0 contain a trifluoromethyl group, 16 a geminal difluoromethylene and 23 any carbon bearing two halogens. No proposal carries a formal charge and none carries specified stereochemistry, matching digest charged_rate 0.0 and stereocentre_rate 0.0 on all five sets, yet structural perception of the same molecules finds unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2,293 of 4,350 (844 of 870 on one objective, 87 of 87 in its top decile) with zero assigned anywhere. 84 proposals have six or fewer heavy atoms and sit at their objective's floor. Full-set scaffold diversity is moderate (176-541 distinct Murcko scaffolds per 870) but every session endgame is one family: the top decile spans 9-52 scaffolds and a single scaffold holds 40 of 87, 30 of 87, 29 of 87 and 24 of 87 on four objectives. Comparison is complete: context.comparison reports child_complete and paired_complete with seeds 0, 1, 2 matched against code Parent n-61b9b3bfb40d, and all fifteen Child and fifteen Parent trajectory files named in the brief are present and readable. transferable_gaps.evidence: Over this node's 4,350 optimizer proposals (five objectives, seeds 0/1/2, 300 accepted records each, read from the fifteen staging trajectories the brief names under /projects/standard/adeshwal/shared/zhou2577/SPIRAL/.worktrees/slot-0/runs/staging), 1,130 contain a halogen bonded to a non-carbon atom and 627 carry one on an aromatic nitrogen, while exactly 0 contain a trifluoromethyl group, 16 a geminal difluoromethylene and 23 any carbon bearing two halogens. The pattern reaches the leaders: 160 of the 435 top-decile molecules carry a heteroatom-halogen bond, including 46 on an amide nitrogen and 58 fluorines on aromatic nitrogen in two different converged families (COc1c(C)c(C)cc2c1cc(C(=O)N(Cl)c1ccccc1)n2NF and CNc1ccc(F)cc1-n1cc2c(c1C1(F)C=CCN1)c(=O)n(F)c(=N)n2F).
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator places halogen on heteroatoms as freely as on carbon and cannot build a polyhalogenated carbon.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Single-halogen substitution is the cheapest edit in the operator set and it is applied without regard to the element it lands on, while no operator iterates halogenation on the same carbon. A task-agnostic generator would make heteroatom-halogen bond formation a distinct, rarely-drawn move rather than a free substitution, and would add a group-level edit that installs CF3, CHF2 or CF2 as one unit, so that halogen enrichment is reachable on carbon instead of only on N and O.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest counters report charged_rate 0.0 and stereocentre_rate 0.0 on all five sets of 870 proposals, and structural perception of the same molecules finds unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2,293 of the 4,350 with zero assigned anywhere; on one objective 844 of 870 proposals and 87 of 87 of its top decile are affected, and the centre in question is the one the score gradient is built on (CCc1c(Br)cc(N)cc1CCN1CCCCNC1(C)c1cccc(Cl)c1).
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits no charged species and no specified stereochemistry even where its own leaders are stereogenic.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The representation as used can express neither configuration nor protonation state, so every sp3 centre the operators build is an undefined mixture and every proposal is a neutral form. A task-agnostic generator would either assign and mutate configuration explicitly at the centres it creates, or declare the proposal set racemic and neutral so that any objective sensitive to enantiomer, diastereomer or ionisation is known to be out of reach.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 146 of the 4,350 proposals contain a ring of four or fewer atoms every atom of which is aromatic - a bond drawn across the interior of an aromatic ring - and 28 of those are in top deciles (COCCc1c2c(c(C(N=O)Nc3cc4c(N=O)cc3-4)c(C)c1C(C)=O)N=C2 and Cc1c2c(=N)n(CF)c(=O)n3c2c-3n1C1(CF)C(O)=CC=C1CCF). Four-membered rings appear in 957 proposals, and on one objective 215 of 870 proposals and 41 of 87 top molecules carry an 8- to 11-membered ring (CCOc1ccc2c(c1)N1CCN(C)CC(=O)N(C)C(=O)C(CC)=C1c1ccccc1O2).
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring-editing operators close bonds across aromatic rings and build three-, four- and 8-to-11-membered rings with no strain or geometry check.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring formation, bridging and contraction are currently validated by valence and canonical identity alone, so any closure that parses is admitted and can be amplified by selection. A task-agnostic generator would gate those operators on ring size and on whether the new bond spans an aromatic system, and would need an explicit ortho-fusion move so that adding ring mass does not default to transannular or medium-ring closures.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Sulfonyl groups appear in 77 of 4,350 proposals and in 0 of the 435 top-decile molecules, carboxylic acids in 56 of 4,350 and 0 of 435, and nitro groups in 0 of 4,350 - yet one of the ten shared initial records in every session carries both a sulfonamide and an acid (COc1cc(F)cc(-c2ccc(C(CC(=O)O)NC(=O)C3CCCN3S(=O)(=O)c3cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c3)cc2)c1), and its sulfonyl descendants survive on only two objectives (76 and 1 of 870) and vanish on the other three. Where polarity is needed the generator instead emits a bare S-H (306 of 4,350) or an N-O or N-N link (170 and 116 of 4,350).
transferable_gaps.gap: No operator forms sulfonyl, carboxyl or nitro functionality, so strongly polar and acidic handles can only be inherited and lost.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The mutation alphabet is single-atom element and halogen swapping plus fragment transfer, which can delete inherited polar groups but cannot synthesise one. A task-agnostic generator needs a small library of attachable polar groups (sulfonyl, sulfonamide, nitrile, carboxyl, acetamide, methoxy) as atomic edits, so that polar surface area is reachable from a non-polar incumbent rather than only decayable from the initial records.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across 4,350 proposals there are 242 nitroso groups, 112 O-O bonds, 306 bare thiols, 305 N-C-N aminals, 992 enamines and 216 N-halogen amides, and these reach the leaders: 33 of 87 top molecules on one objective carry a nitroso group, 62 of 87 on another carry the aminal centre of CCc1c(Br)cc(N)cc1CCN1CCCCNC1(C)c1cccc(Cl)c1, and 46 of 87 on a third carry the halogen on the amide nitrogen itself. The same objectives' lower-scoring molecules show that the rewarded element is the heavy-atom skeleton, not those groups: the amide family scores 0.44 with an N-H amide too (CCc1c(OC)cc2c(c1C)c(Br)c(C(=O)Nc1ccccn1)n2F).
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator substitutes reactive single-heteroatom groups where a stable isostere is the chemistry the gradient is actually rewarding.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Element substitution is unconstrained by any notion of functional-group stability, so the search climbs through groups a chemist would not draw and the surviving pool is biased toward them. A task-agnostic generator would carry a per-group admission filter (or a stability penalty applied before the oracle call) covering heteroatom-heteroatom single bonds, nitroso, aminal and N-halogen amide motifs, and would offer their stable isosteres as the substitution the operator makes instead.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 84 of the 4,350 proposals have six or fewer heavy atoms and every one of them sits at its objective's floor; they are proposed as late as evaluation 289 (FS), 267 (C), 260 (F) and 238 (O), and on one objective the floor is a constant 0.5 that single atoms reach (C, Cl, N=O), so nothing in the feedback discourages them.
transferable_gaps.gap: Deletion and fragmentation operators have no lower size bound, so one- to six-atom species keep consuming oracle calls deep into a session.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Proposal admission checks valence, canonical novelty and duplication but not heavy-atom count, and the surrogate cannot learn a size floor from scores that are flat at the bottom. A task-agnostic generator would reject candidates below a declared heavy-atom count at breeding time, before the budgeted evaluation, which costs no oracle call and cannot encode task identity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Full-set Murcko scaffold counts are 176 to 541 per 870 proposals, but each top decile collapses to 9 to 52 scaffolds with 40 of 87, 30 of 87, 29 of 87 and 24 of 87 on a single scaffold on four objectives. The ties are exact: seven proposals on one objective report 0.438799 and differ only in halogen identity and pyridyl nitrogen position (CCc1c(OC)cc2c(c1C)c(F)c(C(=O)Nc1ccccn1)n2F against CCc1c(OC)cc2c(c1C)c(Cl)c(C(=O)Nc1ccccn1)n2Cl), and nine proposals on another score above 0.99998 while differing only in the para substituent.
transferable_gaps.gap: Late-session proposals are single-atom permutations of one scaffold that the objective cannot separate.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The breeding distribution late in a session is dominated by one-atom peripheral edits on the incumbent scaffold, and such edits return score-identical neighbours that teach the surrogate nothing. A task-agnostic generator would detect that its recent proposals are score-degenerate neighbours of the incumbent and shift operator weight to scaffold-level moves - ring replacement, linker change, fragment exchange - without reading any task identity.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
